To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the HUI3 scoring system has strong theoretical and psychometric properties and is able to predict utility scores based on the direct measurement of preferences.
we have developed a scoring system for HUI3 that provides a practical method of obtaining utility values from HUI3 data and that the HUI3 scoring system has good predictive validity.

1) the HUI3 multiattribute utility function has strong theoretical foundations, 2) the multiattribute utility function is based on the preferences of a representative sample of the general public, and 3) the multiattribute and single attribute utility functions perform well in predicting directly observed utility scores.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and testing of the Health Utilities Index (HUI), a generic measure of health status, health related quality of live (HRQL), and health utility.

the development of preference-based health status classification systems that can be used for the measurement of health related quality of live, the estimation of quality-adjusted life years, and the economic evaluation of health care.

the estimation of a multiattribute utility system for the Health Utilities Mark 3 (HUl3) system of health status classification, and with the evaluation of the predictive validity of that utility system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the HUI3 utility function is a well founded and useful instrument for measuring health status and for estimating utility scores for health states.
the HUI3 scoring system is the only generic multiattribute system that has both strong theoretical foundations and empirical evidence of validity.

the HUI3 is a well-constructed instrument that is capable of measuring health status in a way that is sensitive to the effects of disease and treatment, that is responsive to change, and that is based on the preferences of the general public.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a multi-attribute utility function that is based on a theoretically and empirically well founded model of health.
the HUI3 scoring system is a valid and reliable way of obtaining utility scores based on preferences in the general population.
the HUI3 scoring system has strong theoretical and practical advantages.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to obtain reliable estimates for a multiattribute utility system from community preferences.
the Health Utilities Index (HUI) system is a well-validated and well-accepted measure of health status.
